newsitem.title: USA: Micro Therapeutics gets FDA okay on dialysis brush.
newsitem.headline: Micro Therapeutics gets FDA okay on dialysis brush.

text.p: Micro Therapeutics Inc said Tuesday it has received marketing clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its Cragg Thrombolytic Brush used in the treatment of hemodialysis grafts.
The company said that the product has been designed for rapid interventional clot disruption and dissolution through mechanical mixing of a thrombolytic drug -- urokinase -- with the blood clot.

It said that in clinical studies conducted at five centers in the United States, the brush was shown to dissolve blood clots nearly 40 percent faster than the control procedure while also using less than 50 percent of the thrombolytic agent.
The company believes that, by reducing the procedure time and drug volume, the overall cost for the procedure can be reduced significantly.
It said that there are nearly 181,000 hemodialysis patients in the U.S. that require some form of annual treatment to clear clotted grafts, creating an estimated $90 million potential market.
